SiMR Basis Geometry Ablations: Role of w, Row-Mean Control, Quantile Sparseness (default=0.5, Operating Points 0.5 & 0.8), and ADNI-MCI Anatomical Attribution

This standalone report summarizes the reproducible ablation experiments evaluating (1) the approximate Stiefel retraction weight w = 0.5 in nsa_flow, (2) why un-thresholded PCA initialization without row-mean removal leaves Component 1 (v1) dense, (3) how the R ANTsR::simlr-style quantile sparseness parameter (default=0.5 everywhere in pysimlr, with 0.5 and 0.8 as the two canonical operating points and None available for un-thresholded nsa_flow, inherited by all linear, deep, flow, and sklearn algorithms) enforces explicit cardinality bounds on v1 without losing global predictive power, and (4) the learned cortical thickness networks on ADNI-MCI (N = 1,084).

w = 0.50
Default NSA-Flow sweet spot: EffRank = 3.00, D = 0.0006, 64.8% sparsity in 4.0s (vs. EffRank = 2.02 collapse at w = 0.01)

4. Quantile-Based sparseness Parameter Ablation (default=0.5, Operating Points 0.5 & 0.8 in pysimlr)

By wiring the R ANTsR::simlr quantile sparseness parameter (default=0.5 everywhere, with 0.5 and 0.8 as the two canonical operating points and None for un-thresholded nsa_flow) into pysimlr's shared sparsification layer (simlr_sparseness, LENDNSAEncoder.v, and _finalize_bases, while keeping nsa_flow completely untouched), every linear, deep, flow, and sklearn algorithm inherits quantile sparsity. At sparseness = 0.50 (default), Component 1 sparsity rises from 35.8% to 61.5% (or CogPC1 R2 = 0.1968 for signed bases); at 0.80 it reaches 81.9%; and at 0.85 it achieves CogPC1 R2 = 0.1923 with (9, 9, 9)/62 active DKT cortical regions per component.
